skill.name: deep-research-framework
skill.description: Framework for deep research reports: define the question and tier sources first, cross-verify, then write conclusion-first reports with explicit uncertainty statements. Use when the user asks for a research report, topic investigation, or competitive analysis.
skill.summary: Structure research reports around clear questions, independent sources, dated evidence, and explicit uncertainty.
skill.author: alapha888

content.user_title: Build Research Reports with Traceable Evidence
content.value_statement: Research reports can hide weak sources, stale facts, and unsupported conclusions. This framework guides clear questions, independent verification, and conclusion-first writing with explicit uncertainty.
actual_capabilities: Define one research question and up to three supporting sub-questions.
Classify sources as primary, secondary, or tertiary before searching.
Require independent corroboration for key conclusions and label single-source claims.
Organize reports into core conclusions, evidence sections, and an uncertainty statement.
Date key facts and require sources for every reported number.
Label speculation and identify conditions that would change conclusions.
limitations: Provides written instructions and an outline, not a search engine or executable research tool.
Source access and current information depend on the host assistant and its available tools.
Cannot guarantee source accuracy or independence without examining the underlying evidence.
Does not provide domain-specific analysis methods or replace expert review.

use_cases.title: Compare Competitors
use_cases.description: Structure a competitor comparison around dated product evidence, independent corroboration, and gaps in available information.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Technical Topic
use_cases.description: Prioritize original papers and official documentation, then distinguish supported conclusions from speculation.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Evidence-Based Brief
use_cases.description: Organize a policy question into focused sections with traceable sources and explicit uncertainty.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Research Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a research outline for [topic]. Define one main question, up to three sub-questions, source tiers, and an uncertainty section.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish scope before collecting evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review Source Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these sources for [question]: [sources]. Classify their tiers, check independence, flag undated facts, and identify claims that need corroboration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: evaluate an existing collection of sources.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Comparative Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [option A] and [option B] using [provided evidence]. Lead with conclusions, cite numerical claims, date facts, and mark single-source claims.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn supplied evidence into a structured comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Conclusions and Uncertainty
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this report: [report and sources]. Check source independence, unsupported numbers, speculation, and stale facts. Revise conclusions and state what would invalidate them.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess the evidence supporting an existing report.

output_examples.input: Outline research on whether our team should adopt a new documentation platform.
output: Main question: Does the platform meet our documentation requirements?
Sub-questions: What features are documented? What migration work is required? What costs are supported by current evidence?
Primary sources: Official documentation, pricing pages, and measured trial results.
Uncertainty: Actual migration effort and independent corroboration remain unresolved.

output_examples.input: Assess a vendor availability claim supported by one undated brochure.
output: Conclusion: The vendor availability claim remains a single-source claim.
Evidence: Only one undated vendor brochure was supplied.
Verification gap: No independent measurements or dated supporting documents were provided.
Reassessment condition: Dated operational evidence and independent corroboration could change this conclusion.

best_practices: Set the main question and source tiers before gathering information.
Check that corroborating sources do not repeat the same original source.
Date key facts and state missing evidence, speculation, and reassessment conditions.
anti_patterns: Treating social posts or forum discussions as evidence for core conclusions.
Presenting single-source claims, speculation, or undated facts as established current knowledge.
Listing sources without clear conclusions or hiding unresolved questions.

faq.question: Does this skill search the web automatically?
faq.answer: It defines a research workflow but includes no search implementation. Browsing depends on the host assistant and available tools.

faq.question: Which sources should support conclusions?
faq.answer: Use primary sources and reputable secondary sources. Treat social posts, forums, and aggregators as leads rather than evidence.

faq.question: How many sources does a key conclusion need?
faq.answer: Use at least two independent sources. Multiple sources repeating one origin do not count as independent corroboration.

faq.question: What happens when only one source exists?
faq.answer: Label the conclusion as a single-source claim and note that independent verification is missing.

faq.question: How should outdated information be handled?
faq.answer: Date every key fact. Treat undated information as possibly stale and explain how newer evidence could change the conclusion.

faq.question: What should the final report contain?
faq.answer: Include core conclusions, sections ordered by conclusion, evidence, and sources, plus an uncertainty statement covering missing evidence and reassessment conditions.
